samples: This module provides a single helper that calls an action you supply up to a set number of times and returns the first success. After each failure it records the error, waits about 100 ms plus a random jitter of up to a quarter of that delay, and doubles the delay for the next try. If every attempt fails, it fails with a GaveUp result carrying the attempt count and only the last error message, and it needs permission to use the clock and randomness. One drawback is that it also sleeps after the final failed attempt before giving up, and the sleep, millisecond and random-integer calls it relies on aren't in the language reference I have, so confirm they exist before depending on it.

This module provides one reusable function that runs an action you supply up to a set number of times, returning the first success and otherwise failing with a report of the attempt count and the last error's text. After each failure it pauses, starting at 100 ms and doubling each time, plus a random extra of up to a quarter of the current delay, and it also pauses after the final failed attempt before giving up, which wastes a little time. It needs the time and random permissions, and it uses a few things (the sleep and millisecond helpers, the random integer helper, and the `from 1 to attempts` loop header) that the language reference doesn't list, so confirm it compiles before relying on it.

This module offers one reusable helper that runs an action you supply, up to a chosen number of attempts, and returns the first successful result. After each failure it waits about 100 ms, doubling the wait each time and adding a random extra of up to a quarter of the current delay. If every attempt fails, it gives up with a failure that reports the attempt count and a description of the last error only, and a count of zero or less fails immediately without trying. Two cautions: it also waits after the final failed attempt before giving up, which wastes time, and it needs the time and random permissions. It also uses sleep and millisecond helpers that the documented standard library list doesn't show, so confirm they exist before relying on it.

This module offers one reusable helper that runs an action you supply up to a set number of times and returns the first success. After each failure it waits about 100 ms plus a small random jitter, doubling the wait every time. If every attempt fails, it gives up with an error reporting the attempt count and the last failure message, and it needs the time and random permissions. Before relying on it, note that it also waits after the final failed attempt, which is wasted time, and that the sleep, millisecond-duration and random-integer helpers it uses are not in the documented library list, so it may not compile as written.

This module offers a retry helper that runs a caller-supplied action up to a given number of times. After each failure it waits for a delay that starts at 100 ms and doubles every time, plus a random extra of up to a quarter of the current delay. It returns the first success, or fails with a record of the attempt count and the last error message, which includes the attempt number. Before relying on it, note that it also waits after the final failed attempt, which delays the give-up result for no benefit. Also, the sleep, millisecond-duration and random-integer calls, the function-typed parameter, and the loop header over a range are not in the documented library and syntax, so I can't confirm they exist or compile.
